text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-A five-nation ceasefire monitoring committee will investigate today a weekend incident in which Israeli shelling wounded six civilian villagers in south Lebanon.
-President Hrawi will officially propose the constitutional amendments after one month.
-Some 430 new industrial firms were established in Lebanon in the first eleven months this year, offering jobs for 3,100 workers.
-Judicial authorities finished investigations in the case of a finance ministry official who was killed by accomplices in an embezzlement case at the ministry.
-Minister of Foreign Affairs Bouez met Arab diplomats in Beirut.
-Lebanese ambassador in Washington Tabbarah says Prime Minister Hariri will not meet U.S. President Clinton during the "Friends of Lebanon" conference in Washington on December 16.
-The weekly treasury bill issue of December 5 raised 468.7 bln pounds. The new issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 221 bln pounds.
